concept.name: Tilt
concept.definition: A state of emotional confusion or frustration - the term originates in poker - in which a person abandons sound strategy for suboptimal, usually overly aggressive play. In trading it denotes the degraded decision-making state that follows losses, humiliating outcomes, or provocation, and it also has a 'winner's tilt' variant after unexpected success.
concept.intuition: Tilt is the moment the plan leaves the room: you are no longer trading your system, you are trading your anger.
concept.mechanics: Frustration (typically a loss or bad beat) shifts behavior toward aggression, impulsivity, and larger risk; the standard countermeasures in the poker-derived literature are stopping play, lowering variance, and returning only after emotions subside. Strong positive emotions can produce the same degradation (winner's tilt).
concept.failure_modes: On tilt, risk limits and edge estimates are effectively suspended, so loss severity compounds; because the state feels like urgency and conviction rather than impairment, self-detection usually lags the behavior.
concept.misconceptions: Tilt is not just being upset - it is an observable shift to a worse strategy. It is also not confined to losses: euphoric overconfidence after wins produces the same recklessness.
concept.example: After a stop-out seconds before the market reversed, a trader fires off five marginal trades in twenty minutes, losing more than in the prior two weeks combined.
